**docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-16-human-reply-design.md:82**
* The documented `scripts/` layout omits `corpus.py`, `ai_filter.py`, and `github_records.py`, even though setup invokes all three and they are part of this PR's runtime. The layout is misleading for anyone implementing or auditing the collector; list every script shipped by the skill here.

**skills/team-tooling/human-reply/SKILL.md:118**
* A channel draft may legitimately contain a fenced code or `suggestion` block, but wrapping it in another same-length fenced block makes the inner fence terminate the outer one and changes what the user can paste. Use an outer fence longer than any fence in the draft (or another unambiguous delimiter).
```
After the first line, print the draft in one fenced block with the
channel's markup exactly as it should be pasted, then one line saying
where it goes. Nothing else. For `rewrite`, that line also gives the word
count before and after.
```
**skills/team-tooling/human-reply/scripts/ai_filter.py:59**
* This scans raw lines, so `# ...` inside a fenced code block is counted as a markdown header. A long human-written message containing code comments can therefore gain an AI-pattern hit and be dropped, although the reference defines this detector as a line starting with a markdown header. Exclude fenced-code contents (and other markup-like text inside code) before applying the header/bold-label detector.
```
def headers_bold_labels(text, ctx):
    return any(HEADER.match(line) for line in _lines(text)) or bool(BOLD_LABEL.search(text))

```
**skills/team-tooling/human-reply/scripts/ai_filter.py:54**
* `_lines` removes blank lines before pairing adjacent lines, so `Title:\n\n- item` is treated as a directly labelled list even though the reference definition requires the bullet to follow immediately. This adds false AI-filter hits and can push otherwise human messages over the drop threshold; inspect adjacent raw lines here instead.
```
    lines = _lines(text)
    return any(a.rstrip().endswith(":") and BULLET.match(b) for a, b in zip(lines, lines[1:]))
```
**skills/team-tooling/human-reply/scripts/corpus.py:136**
* On the second hold-out pass, `setup/04-filter.md` supplies `--passed` and says only post-cutoff threads should fill missing slots. This still leaves `pre` as the first pool, so when the first pass found fewer than three pre-cutoff threads, a new pre-cutoff thread can be selected before an eligible post-cutoff thread. Once `passed_ids` is present, use the post-cutoff pool as the only new pool.
```
    pools = [("pre-cutoff", pre)]
    if cutoff is not None and passed_ids is not None:
        post = sorted(t for t, rs in eligible.items()
                      if not any(is_pre_cutoff(r, cutoff) for r in rs)
                      and all(record_id(r) in passed_ids for r in rs))
        pools.append(("post-cutoff", post))
```
**skills/team-tooling/human-reply/scripts/github_records.py:71**
* `by_number` only includes authors who wrote comments returned by `issues/comments`; it never adds the issue or PR author. A first comment by the user on someone else's issue/PR therefore gets `others: 0` and cannot be selected for calibration, even though the issue author is a participant. Include the issue/PR author when building the participant set.
```
def issue_comment_records(comments, login, repo, since, until):
    by_number = commenters(comments, "issue_url")
    return [record("issue comment", c["created_at"], repo, f"{repo}#{number_from_url(c['issue_url'])}",
                   len(by_number[number_from_url(c["issue_url"])] - {login}), c["body"])
```
**skills/team-tooling/human-reply/scripts/github_records.py:112**
* The participant map used for PR bodies is built only from issue comments and review comments, before the submitted reviews are fetched below. A PR authored by the person that has only another user's review summary therefore gets `others: 0`, so `select_holdouts` excludes that conversation even though another participant exists.
```
    others = commenters(issue_comments, "issue_url")
    for number, logins in commenters(review_comments, "pull_request_url").items():
        others.setdefault(number, set()).update(logins)
```
**skills/team-tooling/human-reply/setup/01-detect.md:25**
* The reuse branch creates a fresh `setup.json` with only `reused`/`collected` state, then skips the interview, but later filter/measure/hold-out steps still require the prior cutoff, seed, method, and profile header data. A normal finished setup deletes `setup.json` when the person keeps corpus files, so choosing reuse here leaves those placeholders undefined and cannot resume. Reconstruct the required state from the existing profile/channel headers (and generate a seed) or rerun the interview before marking the channel collected.
**skills/team-tooling/human-reply/setup/03-collect.md:118**
* The GitHub path does not enforce the 1,500-record cap until after every discovered repository has been collected. `github_records.py` paginates all comments and PRs for each repo first, so users with large histories can spend substantial time and disk space writing a corpus that is immediately truncated, and the in-memory lists can grow without the stated cap. Normalize/check the remaining capacity after each repo and stop collection once the cap is reached.
**skills/team-tooling/human-reply/setup/03-collect.md:91**
* `select_holdouts` treats any record with `others >= 1` as a qualifying multi-person thread, but this assigns `others: 1` to every thread reply (and every top-level post with replies), including a user replying only to their own thread. Such a thread can be held out and then discarded during calibration, reducing or eliminating valid calibration examples. Populate this from the actual distinct non-user authors, using `0` when the participant count is unknown.
**skills/team-tooling/human-reply/setup/03-collect.md:72**
* The newest month is allowed to run through the first day of the next month, so when `window.until` is mid-month this query collects messages after the requested window and lets them affect filtering and budgets. Clamp the newest window's `before` boundary to the day after `window.until`.
**skills/team-tooling/human-reply/setup/04-filter.md:109**
* The no-Python branch explicitly records dropped ids instead of writing a kept JSONL, but the next measure/read steps unconditionally use `<channel>.kept.jsonl` (and the borrow reader uses its kept file too). A setup run without Python therefore cannot reach the reader stage unless it invents a file that this branch never creates; make the later steps read the original corpus while applying `dropped`, or materialize the kept files consistently.
**skills/team-tooling/human-reply/setup/06-read.md:53**
* Three readers can all fail validation twice, but this branch then says to use “the one remaining return” even when zero returns remain. The merge and calibration steps have no defined input in that case; explicitly mark the channel unusable/partial or define a no-reader fallback.
**skills/team-tooling/human-reply/setup/07-calibrate.md:76**
* Earlier in this step, threads whose fetched context contains nobody but the person are dropped. If that removes the last held-out thread, there is no "first remaining held-out thread" to re-draft, yet this branch still asks the acceptance question and records `accepted`/`rejected`. Handle the empty set by selecting a replacement or marking calibration skipped/partial instead of claiming acceptance without a draft.
**skills/team-tooling/human-reply/setup/07-calibrate.md:42**
* The `issue comment` surface includes comments on ordinary GitHub issues, but this calibration branch always runs `gh pr view`. For a held-out issue comment, that command fails because the number is not a PR, so no context or draft can be produced; use the issue endpoint for issue threads or detect whether the number is a PR first.

Verify settled-item coverage before exempting an answer `skills/​pr-tooling/​pr-autopilot/​steps/​02-preflight-review.md:216` Step 1 allows a `no` that names a nonexistent or non-covering settled item to survive if it meets the ordinary citation rule. Queue both initial and re-ask batches under a host-aware concurrency limit, as `pr-loop-lib/steps/04-dispatch-fixers.md:45–65` does for fixers. Retry capacity refusals without consuming the evidence re-ask, with a bounded fallback when no running reviewer can free a slot.
